title: Good results, bad week: the AI sell-off pushes stocks into a correction

questions.q: On Monday the Nasdaq closed about 10.9% below its October 6 high. On Friday the Nasdaq-100 closed 19.84% below its record close. Which labels fit?
options: Both were already in a bear market
Neither label applies until the Fed acts
The Nasdaq was in a correction on Monday, and by Friday the Nasdaq-100 was just short of a bear market
Monday was a bear market and Friday was a correction
questions.explain: A {{market-correction|correction}} is a fall of 10% or more from a peak; a {{bear-market|bear market}} is 20% or more. Friday's close left the Nasdaq-100 49.41 points above the bear market line.

questions.q: On Tuesday St. Louis Fed President Musalem said he wants the real interest rate between 2% and 2.5% by spring and estimated it is about a full point below that now. What does that imply?
options: The Fed needs to raise its rate, or inflation needs to fall, to close the gap
The Fed should cut rates right away
Inflation is already below zero
Treasury yields must rise to 2%
questions.explain: The {{real-interest-rate|real interest rate}} is the Fed's rate minus inflation. If it is a point too low, the Fed would need more {{rate-hike|rate hikes}}, which is why CNBC reported Musalem sees as many as four.

questions.q: On Thursday gold fell 3.04% and on Friday 4.63%, to a 14.5-month low, while stocks tumbled both days. What makes that unusual?
options: Gold usually moves exactly with oil
Gold cannot be traded on Fridays
Gold always rises when bitcoin falls
Gold is normally treated as a safe haven that investors buy when they are frightened
questions.explain: A {{safe-haven|safe haven}} is something investors buy in a panic. On Thursday Capp Notes blamed a strong dollar and hike bets. On Friday the dollar slipped and yields fell, and the sources read did not explain the drop.

questions.q: Anthropic sold shares at $83, closed its first day at $97.17, and ended Friday at about $88 to $89. What happened to its IPO pop?
options: It grew to more than 30%
Most of it was given back, but the shares stayed above the $83 IPO price
It turned into a loss for everyone who bought at the IPO price
It cannot be measured until a year after the listing
questions.explain: An {{ipo-pop|IPO pop}} is measured from the {{ipo|IPO}} price. The 17% first-day gain shrank to roughly 6% to 7% as AI stocks sold off on Friday.

questions.q: On Tuesday Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103%, and guided to about $130 billion. By Friday the stock had fallen 14% in a day. Which reading of the week fits the briefs?
options: The results were later revised down by the company
Nvidia missed its revenue forecast
Strong results were outweighed by legal and regulatory risks: a California subpoena and a reported SEC look at its accounting
Interest rates were cut, which hurt growth stocks
questions.explain: Results answer how the business is doing; an {{sec-investigation|SEC investigation}} and a subpoena raise questions about risk that results cannot settle. Since Huang's exit the briefs have tracked this as {{key-person-risk|key-person risk}} plus legal risk.

questions.q: On Monday the 10-year Treasury yield fell 3 basis points to 5.12%, on Thursday 3 to 5.04%, and on Friday 12 to 4.92%. On Tuesday Musalem called for more hikes, and on Wednesday the Fed's minutes read hawkish. Why did yields fall anyway?
options: The Fed bought bonds on each of those days
Each fall came on a day of heavy stock selling, when investors moved money into Treasuries
The Treasury stopped selling new bonds
Inflation data showed prices falling
questions.explain: A {{flight-to-safety|flight to safety}} pushes bond prices up and {{treasury-yield|yields}} down. On these days fear about stocks outweighed {{hawkish|hawkish}} Fed talk, which on its own would push yields up.

questions.q: Monday's brief covered a new US rule on remote access to AI chips, Thursday's a short seller's claim about AMD and a blacklisted Chinese company, and Friday's a California subpoena about whether chips reached China. What links the three?
options: All three are about oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz
All three are about Fed interest-rate decisions
All three concern a company's IPO
All three involve export controls, the limits on selling advanced US chips to China
questions.explain: {{export-controls|Export controls}} restrict which customers chipmakers can serve. Each story raised the chance of lost sales or penalties, which is why chip stocks fell on all three days.

questions.q: Consumer staples rose 0.3% on Monday and 0.67% on Friday, the only sector up that day, while technology led the losses. What pattern does that show?
options: Money moving from AI-linked stocks into defensive ones whose sales hold up in any economy
Staples companies reported record AI revenue
Staples stocks always rise on Mondays and Fridays
Staples rose because oil prices fell to zero
questions.explain: {{defensive-stocks|Defensive stocks}} such as food and household goods makers tend to hold up in sell-offs. The weak {{market-breadth|market breadth}} on both days shows the selling was wide, but staples were spared.
